meta.description: Generates 3D conformer ensembles using RDKit ETKDGv3 with knowledge-enhanced distance geometry, MMFF94/UFF force-field optimization, CREST + GFN2-xTB semi-empirical refinement, and macrocycle-aware torsion preferences. Provides explicit decision rules for single vs ensemble conformer use, RMSD pruning, energy windows, conformer count, and force-field choice. Use when preparing 3D ligands for docking, generating descriptor input for 3D QSAR, or sampling macrocycle/peptide conformational ensembles.

scientific_integrity.detail: All cited references (Riniker & Landrum 2015 JCIM, Wang et al. 2020 ETKDGv3, Halgren 1996 MMFF94, Rappe 1992 UFF, Pracht et al. 2024 CREST 3.0, Bannwarth/Ehlert/Grimme 2019 GFN2-xTB, Hawkins et al. 2010 OMEGA) are real, verifiable papers with correct DOIs. No fabricated data, statistics, or results in any of the 7 executed outputs.

practice_boundaries.detail: Skill is a pure computational-chemistry geometry tool (molecular conformer generation); no diagnostic, prescriptive, or patient-facing content appears anywhere, so no medical disclaimer is applicable.

methodological_ground.detail: No methodological fallacy detected. Adversarial probe (Input 7) confirmed the skill's own framing does not support a 'global minimum with certainty' claim -- reported minima are correctly the best-of-n-sampled value, consistent with SKILL.md's own caveats about Boltzmann populations being 'exploratory surrogates, not generally validated populations.'

code_usability.detail: All 7 code paths executed to completion without unhandled crashes; every path either ran correctly or failed with a real, traceable exception (CREST FileNotFoundError in Input 6; ArgumentError from an unguarded mol=None in Input 7). No syntax errors, infinite loops, or unexplained missing-dependency failures. The unguarded-input case (Input 7) is a real defect but is runnable code with a real (if unfriendly) exception, not the unrunnable-code condition this gate targets -- recorded instead as a P1 code-quality recommendation.

functional_suitability.note: All promised methods (ETKDGv3, MMFF94/UFF, RMSD pruning, energy windows, macrocycle handling, CREST+GFN2-xTB, Boltzmann averaging) are covered and mostly accurate; the CREST Prerequisites line gives no Windows caveat even though CREST has no Windows build at all (verified: FileNotFoundError, no conda-forge win-64 package).

reliability.note: Strong failure-mode/common-errors tables, but the SKILL.md-body gen_conformers() omits the 'mol is None' guard that macrocycle_conformers() and crest_workflow() both include elsewhere in the same file; confirmed to raise an opaque C++ ArgumentError on malformed SMILES instead of a clear ValueError.

performance_context.note: Reasonable progressive disclosure via usage-guide.md + examples/gen_conformers.py, though a fair amount of full code is duplicated inline in SKILL.md rather than solely referenced from the examples file.

agent_usability.note: Clear decision tree and version-compatibility guidance; confirmed function-name mismatch between SKILL.md (gen_conformers, prune_conformers_rmsd, filter_by_energy) and examples/gen_conformers.py (gen_conformer_ensemble, prune_rmsd, filter_energy_window) for the same operations.

human_usability.note: Natural example prompts in usage-guide.md match how a researcher would actually ask; version-drift adaptation guidance ('introspect the installed package') is a genuine forgiveness strength.

security.note: No credentials, no eval/exec of raw strings, subprocess calls use list-form args (not shell strings). Input validation is inconsistent across the skill's own functions (see reliability note).

maintainability.note: Clean per-topic modular sections (Goal/Approach/code each); no shipped assertion-based tests, only a printing __main__ demo, verified to run correctly.

agent_specific.note: Precise trigger description; clean 'Related Skills' composability section; confirmed bit-identical idempotency under a fixed seed. Escape-hatch guidance for organometallics/unusual chemistry is present but thin.

recommendations.title: CREST + GFN2-xTB workflow is unrunnable on Windows with no documented caveat
recommendations.problem: The documented `crest xtbopt.xyz --gfn2 --T 12 --ewin 6` command fails with FileNotFoundError because CREST publishes no Windows build anywhere upstream (Linux binaries only, no win-64 conda-forge package). The Prerequisites section's `conda install -c conda-forge xtb crest` line gives no indication this half of the install will silently fail to resolve on Windows.
recommendations.root_cause: The Skill was written/tested assuming a Unix-like environment and does not distinguish xtb (which does have a Windows build and was confirmed working) from CREST (which does not).
recommendations.fix: Add an explicit platform note to Prerequisites and to the 'CREST + GFN2-xTB for High-Quality Sampling' section: CREST requires Linux/macOS or WSL; on native Windows, fall back to RDKit ETKDGv3 macrocycle-aware embedding (already documented elsewhere in the Skill) or a WSL-hosted CREST install.

recommendations.title: gen_conformers() in SKILL.md lacks the None-guard used elsewhere in the same file
recommendations.problem: Calling the SKILL.md-documented gen_conformers() on an unparseable SMILES raises an opaque boost.python ArgumentError from Chem.AddHs(None) instead of a clear error, even though malformed/missing SMILES are a routine occurrence in the batch workflows the usage-guide explicitly promotes ('for each compound in library.csv').
recommendations.root_cause: macrocycle_conformers() and crest_workflow() both include `if mol is None: raise ValueError(...)`, but the ETKDGv3 section's gen_conformers() omits the same guard -- an inconsistency within the Skill's own code, not a missing capability.
recommendations.fix: Add `if mol is None: raise ValueError(f'Invalid SMILES: {smiles!r}')` immediately after `Chem.MolFromSmiles(smiles)` in the SKILL.md gen_conformers() code block, matching the pattern already used in macrocycle_conformers() and crest_workflow().

recommendations.title: Function names differ between SKILL.md and examples/gen_conformers.py for the same operations
recommendations.problem: SKILL.md uses gen_conformers/prune_conformers_rmsd/filter_by_energy while the shipped examples/gen_conformers.py uses gen_conformer_ensemble/prune_rmsd/filter_energy_window for the equivalent operations, with no cross-reference noting the rename.
recommendations.root_cause: The reference example was evidently refactored independently of the SKILL.md prose.
recommendations.fix: Align names between SKILL.md and examples/gen_conformers.py (pick one canonical set), or add a one-line note where each is introduced pointing to its counterpart.

recommendations.title: Macrocycle-aware embedding's claimed benefit has no worked before/after example
recommendations.problem: Testing useMacrocycleTorsions=True on a genuine >=12-atom ring found default ETKDGv3 settings succeeded equally (50/50) on the same simple carbocyclic test molecule, so the documented claim that 'ETKDGv3 default knowledge base under-samples macrocycle torsions' is not demonstrated by any example in the Skill itself.
recommendations.root_cause: No worked example compares macrocycle-aware vs. default settings on a genuinely difficult macrocycle (e.g. the cyclosporine A case named in usage-guide.md but never coded).
recommendations.fix: Add a concrete before/after example (e.g. cyclosporine A or another stereochemically constrained macrocycle) showing embedding failure or degraded diversity under default settings versus success under useMacrocycleTorsions=True.
